evidence.finding: Executor tried repeatedly to bootstrap the originally-provisioned mariadb-server/galera-3 stack (empty gcomm:// address, then restoring saved 60-galera.cnf) but mysql.service kept failing to start ('control process exited with error code'); mysqld socket never appeared.

After purging mariadb-server/galera-3 and installing percona-xtradb-cluster-server-5.6 + percona-galera-3, two large apt-get install commands each hit the platform's 120s proxy read timeout, leaving background apt/dpkg processes that had to be killed with kill -9 and repaired with 'dpkg --configure -a' before proceeding.

After the PXC install succeeded, all three nodes started mysql successfully and joined as a working 3-node Galera cluster (wsrep_cluster_size 3, status Primary, wsrep_ready ON), with matching row/checksum data on all nodes.

Executor took a pre-maintenance baseline (checksum matched on all 3 nodes), inserted a new row ('widget-4-pre-maintenance') on node2, then cleanly stopped mysql on all three nodes in sequence (node3, node2, node1) and confirmed node1's grastate.dat recorded seqno 7 with safe_to_bootstrap: 1.
All three nodes confirmed fully stopped (systemctl inactive, no mysqld process) — the maintenance-window shutdown itself completed successfully.

Executor checked wsrep_cluster_address (correctly still gcomm://10.100.61.10,10.100.61.11,10.100.61.12) and ran 'galera_new_cluster', which was not found ('command not found') — PXC 5.6 apparently doesn't ship that MariaDB-specific bootstrap wrapper.
Cluster lease expired at 15:24:55.382Z, ~9 seconds after the last command and before any bootstrap of the stopped cluster was attempted or completed.

likely_causes.cause: The lease/time budget was exhausted primarily by early struggles getting the originally-provisioned mariadb-server + galera-3 stack to start at all, followed by a costly mid-task decision to purge it and install percona-xtradb-cluster-server-5.6 instead — two of those install attempts each burned the full 120s proxy timeout plus manual recovery (kill -9, dpkg --configure -a).

Once switched to PXC 5.6, the executor assumed the MariaDB-specific 'galera_new_cluster' convenience script would be available for bootstrapping after full shutdown; it was not, so the actual bootstrap of the stopped cluster (starting node1 first with wsrep_new_cluster / bootstrap option, then joining node2 and node3) was never attempted before the lease expired.

The clean full shutdown itself succeeded and node1's grastate.dat shows a consistent, safe-to-bootstrap state (seqno 7, safe_to_bootstrap: 1), so the data and shutdown procedure were not the problem — only the restart/bootstrap step was missing when the run ended.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, first determine (early, before spending much time) whether the provisioned image's stock mariadb-server + galera-3 packages actually start as a single-node bootstrap (`wsrep_cluster_address="gcomm://"`, `systemctl start mysql`) — if it fails, capture `journalctl -xe -u mysql` and the mysqld error log immediately rather than iterating blindly, since diagnosing that root cause may avoid the costly full package swap seen in this attempt.

If a distro/package swap to Percona XtraDB Cluster (or any large package set) is genuinely required, run apt-get install in the background-and-poll pattern (`cmd > /tmp/out.log 2>&1 & echo $! > pid; tail -f via polling`) instead of one synchronous exec, since installs here exceeded the platform's 120s proxy timeout twice and each failure required manual dpkg/apt recovery.

Before shutting the cluster down for the maintenance window, confirm in advance which bootstrap mechanism the installed package actually provides (MariaDB packages typically ship `galera_new_cluster`; Percona XtraDB Cluster 5.6 instead uses `service mysql bootstrap-pxc` or starting mysqld with `--wsrep-new-cluster` / a temporary empty `gcomm://` address) so the restart step is not discovered for the first time after full shutdown.

After full shutdown, bootstrap only the node with the highest `seqno` and `safe_to_bootstrap: 1` in grastate.dat (node1 had seqno 7 here) — start that node alone first, verify `wsrep_cluster_size=1`/`wsrep_cluster_status=Primary`, then start mysql normally on the other two nodes so they rejoin via IST/SST with the full gcomm address list restored.

Keep the good practices already demonstrated: pre-shutdown baseline checksums on all nodes, verifying grastate.dat's safe_to_bootstrap flag, and sequential clean shutdown — these should be preserved in the next attempt, just followed through to a completed restart with time held in reserve for the final bootstrap+rejoin sequence.
summary: The maintenance-window shutdown itself succeeded — all three nodes were cleanly stopped with consistent data and a safe-to-bootstrap grastate.dat on node1 (seqno 7) — but the cluster was never brought back up. The lease expired 9 seconds after the executor discovered mid-restart that 'galera_new_cluster' (the bootstrap helper it expected) was not available on this Percona XtraDB Cluster 5.6 install. Most of the attempt's time appears to have been consumed earlier by (a) failed attempts to start the originally-provisioned mariadb-server/galera-3 stack and (b) a subsequent switch to installing percona-xtradb-cluster-server-5.6, where two install commands each hit the platform's 120s proxy timeout and required manual dpkg/process recovery. Net result: outage was never resolved within the lease window — the fresh attempt should end with a running, rejoined 3-node cluster, not just a clean shutdown.</summary>
